what: Murphy USA runs about 1,750 petrol stations, most of them on Walmart car parks, selling fuel at low prices and making much of its profit on the cigarettes, drinks and snacks sold inside.
customers: American drivers filling up, mostly value-conscious ones shopping at Walmart.
money: tobacco, drinks, snacks and prepared food
moat: Sites on the car parks of the busiest retailer in America, with fuel priced to pull traffic and merchandise margins that pay the bills. The locations themselves cannot be matched.
risks: Fuel margins per gallon swing with crude prices and competition
Cigarettes are a large share of merchandise profit and volumes decline every year
opportunities: 14.3 times earnings and 13.8 times free cash flow with $668M of free cash flow
Analysts see about 20% upside, with 11 covering the stock
The company buys back a large share of its stock every year, which has driven earnings per share far faster than revenue
watch: Fuel margin per gallon and merchandise sales excluding tobacco.
